newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $1.621 bln trade gap Jan 1-Feb 23.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $1.621 bln trade gap Jan 1-Feb 23.

text.p: Brazil posted a trade deficit of $1.621 billion between January 1 and February 23, Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, the Finance Ministry's Economic Policy Secretary, said.
Exports during the period totalled $5.951 billion while imports were $7.572 billion, Mendonca de Barros told reporters.

Problems with a new, computerized system to record imports, which hampered January's trade balance, had been solved and the $1.621 billion figure was a "true" reflection of Brazil's trade deficit in the first 35 working days of 1997, the official said.
Newspapers have reported that Brazil would post a trade deficit of $1.5 billion in February alone, due mostly to oil imports from January that were only registered this month.
In January, Brazil reported a $413 million trade deficit.
